name: Toy branched steady-state flux feasibility
description: Find a feasible nonnegative steady-state flux vector for two internal pools linked by parallel branches, under authored capacities and a branch-B requirement. No optimal flux or organism prediction is claimed.
assumptions: Toy network: inlet supplies internal pool X; branches A and B each transfer one X to one Y; outlet removes Y. Stoichiometric rows are [1,-1,-1,0] and [0,1,1,-1].
Fixed-volume steady state with no accumulation of the two internal pools; external inlet/outlet are allowed. Conservation constraints are S*v=0, not equality of all individual fluxes.
Uniform scale 10 uM/s: q=v/10. Capacity offsets 1,0.8,0.6,1 correspond to 10,8,6,10 uM/s. Branch-B minimum offset -0.3 enforces v_B>=3 uM/s.
All flux limits and initial values are illustrative authored numbers. No real metabolites, organism, measured kinetic constants or reconstructed biological network are identified.
Nonnegative variables declare irreversible branch directions; thermodynamic feasibility, kinetics and enzyme availability are not inferred from steady-state balance alone.
This task finds constraint feasibility. It has no biomass, ATP or other linear objective and therefore does not claim a conventional FBA optimum.
One explicit feasible witness is [9,6,3,9]. The source paper supports the S*v=0 framework; the toy topology and numerical bounds are newly authored.
